messages.content: Predict a human choice between left and right allocations in the initial dictator-game phase. The participant chooses between two colored pie charts representing how 3 euros are split between themselves and another anonymous person. The other person cannot reject or return anything. Choose the left pie with Q or the right pie with P; choices are self-paced. There are 55 recorded allocation decisions after four practice trials. At the end, one decision is randomly selected for the participant's own allocation bonus; this cohort does not also receive the other-person allocation bonus used in the earlier study. The later observation and time-perception tasks have separate bonuses, revealed only at the end; their later results are unavailable for this earlier choice. The record expresses the original pie sizes as quantities: drawing code rounds 3 times each stored allocation ratio to one decimal euro, then divides by 3 for the own colored wedge. The complementary wedge belongs to the other person. These numbers encode the diagram; exact numerical labels were not drawn on each decision screen. Actual payment calculation uses the underlying allocation ratio, whose finer precision is not included here. Original per-person colors and fixed fee are unavailable; that does not imply the participant lacked them. Fifteen Social Value Orientation allocation questions occurred before this phase; their answers and the four practice choices are unavailable. Every earlier recorded own allocation and action is supplied in order. History columns t,L_self_tenths_EUR,R_self_tenths_EUR,choice give the earlier trial number, graphical own shares in tenths of a euro, and left/right action; each other share is 30 minus the own value in the same unit. No current response time, later fitted preference or future response is included. Individually linked demographic attributes are unavailable and have not been imputed. Return only left or right.
